Let me approach this from my knowledge of crystallography:

In crystallography, Z represents the number of formula units in the unit cell. When molecules are located on special positions (positions with site symmetry), the effective number of molecules can be reduced because they are related by symmetry operations.

If Z is half the expected amount, this suggests that molecules are located on a symmetry element that has a multiplicity of 2. Among the given options:

A. Fourfold rotation axes - These would reduce Z to 1/4 of the expected value
B. Glide planes - These are translational symmetry elements that don't reduce Z in this way
C. Inversion centers - When molecules are located on inversion centers, Z is reduced by a factor of 2
D. Twofold screw axes - These are translational symmetry elements that don't reduce Z in this way

The inversion center (option C) is the only symmetry element among the options that would reduce Z by a factor of 2. When a molecule is located on an inversion center, half of its atoms are related to the other half by the inversion operation, effectively reducing the number of independent molecules by a factor of 2.

Final Answer: [ANSWER]C[/ANSWER]
